text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Crown Prince Hassan and Prime Minister Majali meet U.S. deputy chief of staff.
- Supply minister says ministry will focus on monitoring food quality, providing strategic reserves, and setting prices to avoid monopolies.
- Marked improvement in Iraqi dinar exchange rate on local market.
- Opposition deputies call for a halt to normalisation and joint projects with Israel.
- King Hussein and Arafat to open a conference on Jerusalem in Amman in early April.
- First tranche of Gulf War compensation worth 321,000 dinars ($453,000) arrives.
- Customs seize 215 kg (470 pounds) of gold smuggled into Jordan.
- New minister of culture says he didn't touch the Koran when he was sworn in because he was not clean.
- Iraq's borders open up to Jordanian goods. Jordanian companies which won contracts under the oil-for-food deal start to export to Baghdad. Trade across Iraq's border with Turkey also picks up.
- Supply minister says there will be regular meetings with the private sector to remove obstacles to business.
- King and Clinton to meet on April 1.
- Prime minister pledges close cooperation with parliament.
